Life at Hay was made as bearable as conditions allowed. Boredom was overcome by paid work, hobbies, sport and camp entertainment. This is a programme for a concert held at the Hay Camp, directed and arranged by M. Pietruschka. The concert featured the works of Delibres, Czibulka, Rimsky-Korsakov, Brahms, Dvorak, Boccherin, Gounod, Paganini and Strauss. Performers included M. Pietruschka (violin), Mr. Chlumecky (violin), Mr Silberstein (violin), Mr Goldmann-Petersen (violin), Mr Landauer (guitar), Mr Gurland (flute) and Mr Ehrenzweig (bass). Mr. S Cohn was the manager of the concert, while Mr E. Wittenberg was the stage manager. Mr Ehrenzweig also sang two ballads, "Prince Eugen" and "The Campbells are Commin'".

Russian-born Ivan Pietruschka was a talented violinist and conductor in Eastern Europe. In 1939 he sought refuge in England, but was soon declared an “enemy alien” by the British and sent to Australia on the H.M.T Dunera with approximately 2000 other Jewish refugees of German and Austrian descent. Interned with other refugees at Hay Camp, Ivan performed regular concerts alongside other interned musicians, Peter Stadlen and Hans Werner Katz. Ivan joined the 8th Employment Company in 1942, created so internees could help with the war effort, before being discharged in 1943. In 1952, Ivan joined the Victorian Symphony Orchestra, now a naturalised Australian.
